insight.title: Why You Keep Finding Problems When Things Go Well
insight.subtitle: How your brain invents new issues as soon as you solve the old ones

sections.text: When a neighborhood becomes safer, residents often report more "suspicious" activity. Your brain doesn’t relax when problems disappear; it simply lowers the threshold for what it considers a problem to keep itself busy.
In a famous study, people shown blue dots eventually labeled purple dots as "blue" once the actual blue dots vanished. Your mind is wired to maintain a steady level of concern, regardless of reality.
This explains why a minor typo feels like a disaster on a quiet day. If you don't recognize this pattern, you will spend your life fixing imaginary issues that don’t actually matter.
Try this today: The next time you find a minor flaw today, ask if it actually matters.
High standards are useful, but hunting for ghosts is an expensive use of your attention.

news.title: IMF drops Eurozone's economic growth forecast to 1.1% from 1.4% amid Iran war
news.description: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has adjusted its growth projection for the eurozone down to 1.1% from 1.4% for 2026 as prospects for the euro area dwindle amid higher inflation and reduced momentum.
news.why: Your job prospects may weaken as business expansion slows across Europe.

news.why: You may face higher prices at the pump due to restricted oil supplies.

news.title: How Will US Navy’s Strait Of Hormuz Blockade Impact Iran And Its Economy?
news.description: Iran has weathered decades of US sanctions and regional conflicts, but Washington’s naval blockade could still disrupt its oil exports, trade flows and economic stability.
news.why: The variety of imported goods available to you may decrease significantly.

news.title: SpaceX, Blue Origin in focus after NASA’s Artemis success
news.description: After the safe return of four astronauts from a historic flyby of the moon last week, NASA is shifting focus to its next challenge: putting competing lunar landers from Elon Musk’s SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin through a series of rigorous tests ahead of future crewed landings.
news.why: Public tax dollars may shift toward funding new commercial space projects.

news.title: 'Big Short' Legend Steve Eisman Says Buying Software Stocks Is 'Just Like Catching A Falling Knife'

news.why: Your retirement savings could fluctuate as software company stock values drop.

news.title: Two new TB vaccine candidates show promise but fail to stop infection
news.description: A large trial in India suggests the VPM1002 and Immuvac vaccine candidates are safe and may reduce the risk of active tuberculosis in adults and older children, but do not prevent infection or transmission.
news.why: Healthcare options for treating serious lung infections may change your medical outlook.
